blogs.title: The Staleness Problem: Updating FOIA Declarations in Long-Running Investigations
blogs.description: This post analyzes the D.C. Circuit's application of the 'pending or reasonably anticipated' standard under FOIA Exemption 7(A). It examines how the court resolved the tension between the need for current evidence and the reality of long-term counterterrorism investigations, specifically regarding the sufficiency of updated declarations when significant time has passed since the initial withholding.

blogs.title: Behind Closed Doors: Ex Parte Submissions and the Segregability Inquiry
blogs.description: This post examines the procedural dynamics of FOIA litigation involving national security. It focuses on the court's reliance on ex parte declarations to determine segregability, the 'inextricably intertwined' standard, and the inherent challenges for plaintiffs challenging sealed submissions when the very information sought is at issue.

blogs.title: Heightened Deference: National Security and the Law Enforcement Purpose Prong
blogs.description: This post explores the level of judicial deference afforded to the FBI when invoking FOIA exemptions in counterterrorism contexts. It discusses the 'law enforcement purpose' requirement and how the court applied precedents like Campbell and CNSS to uphold the agency's determination regarding the nexus between the investigation and national security duties.
